fixtures: Arrival uses fresh constructor position; casts/fights use shoreline fixture. Actual casts and recorded fights; NPCs retained; finite tap strokes; no invented fish pose

visualReview.method: All 18 screenshots were previously inspected. After the controller-only removal of reeling-driven actionFocus, the entire gate was recaptured: 17 final PNGs are byte-identical to their inspected versions; the changed Pacifica phone cast pair was inspected again. Its short-cast camera centre settled slightly differently with identical physics state and scale. Arrival preserves the fresh constructor player position. Cast and fight states use the real simulation, mounted Carolina rigs, fixed sea state, and retained NPCs. Only transient toast notifications are hidden for screenshots.
findings: All 24 recorded conditions passed browser-error, mounted-bottom-rig, renderer-state-mutation and safe-viewport assertions. Angler, rod tip, water entry and visible fish fit within the measured rectangle clear of the interface.

The beach views retain continuous coastal bands and fine foam/terrain detail without magnified terrain cells. Full casts widen to show the actual line span; near fights return to a closer view without enlarging the fish independently.
True Pacifica and Half Moon Bay arrivals show crisp kiosks, correctly attached shop shadows, restrained kelp size and readable shoreline context. Wave foam no longer paints over their roofs.

True Benicia arrival shows both pier sides and the nearby coast. Its shadow remains translucent with ground texture visible, and its land barrier has human-scale posts. No vertical water-coverage seam is visible in the final Benicia images.

All 19 Benicia crowd members remain in simulation state; nearby anglers, coolers, lamps, benches and riprap retain coherent proportions. Bottom rigs have no float marker. The Pacifica near-fight fish is hidden at its actual depth; actual surface fish in Half Moon Bay and Benicia remain small.

notes.observation: The neighbouring NPC line is more visually prominent than the player line during a short cast. It remains attached to its own angler and is not an erroneous player strand.

The broad pier apron remains intentionally sparse and geometric. The phone arrival player is 16.1 CSS px tall to include the pier width and coastline; active short-cast/near-fight views restore about 26.8 CSS px.

performance.method: 18 consecutive warm renderer calls per condition in headless Chrome on the development host; no mobile CPU emulation.
performance.limitations: These timings measure rendering calls, not full interactive device frame pacing.

limitations: The gate samples one fixed sea state and one representative bottom rig. It does not claim an exhaustive review of every camera path, weather state, species or equipment setup.

controllerRecapture.reason: Remove the controller option that allowed reel clicks to boost camera focus.
controllerRecapture.findings: No visual regression in the changed cast pair. All safe UI rectangle and physics-preservation assertions passed again.
